## 2. Pelvic parameters (lateral standing radiograph including the femoral heads)
| Parameter | Definition | Normal | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pelvic incidence (PI)** | Angle between the line perpendicular to the **S1 endplate at its midpoint** and the line from that midpoint to the **centre of the femoral heads (hip axis)** | About **50-55 degrees** (range about 35-85) | **Fixed morphological parameter** after skeletal maturity (does not change with position); **determines the lumbar lordosis a person needs** |
| **Pelvic tilt (PT)** | Angle between the vertical and the line from the hip axis to the S1 endplate midpoint | **Under about 20 degrees** (about 10-20) | **Positional**; **increases (pelvic retroversion) to compensate for sagittal imbalance** |
| **Sacral slope (SS)** | Angle between the S1 endplate and the horizontal | About 35-45 degrees | Positional; decreases with retroversion |

- **Key equation: PI = PT + SS** (geometric).
- **High PI** (large pelvis): needs **more lumbar lordosis**; associated with **isthmic spondylolisthesis** (shear at L5-S1), and with progression of high-grade slips.
- **Low PI**: flatter spine, less lordosis; associated with **Scheuermann**-like flat types and disc degeneration/herniation (Roussouly type 1-2).

## 3. Spinal parameters
- **Lumbar lordosis (LL):** Cobb angle **L1 to S1** (about 40-60 degrees; **two-thirds of lordosis between L4 and S1**).
- **Thoracic kyphosis (TK):** T4 (or T5) to T12, about **20-50 degrees**.
- **Sagittal vertical axis (SVA):** horizontal distance from the **C7 plumb line** to the **posterosuperior corner of S1**: **normal under about 4-5 cm** (positive = C7 anterior to S1). **Over 5 cm = positive sagittal imbalance** (disability rises steeply).
- **T1 pelvic angle (TPA):** angle between the line from the femoral heads to T1 centroid and the line from the femoral heads to the S1 endplate midpoint; combines SVA and PT and is **independent of posture compensation** (target **under about 14-20 degrees**).
- **Cervical parameters:** C2-C7 lordosis, **C2-C7 SVA (cSVA; under about 4 cm)**, **T1 slope minus cervical lordosis (T1S-CL under about 20 degrees)**, chin-brow vertical angle (CBVA: horizontal gaze; important in ankylosing spondylitis osteotomy planning).
- **Global alignment and proportion (GAP) score** (Yilgor): relative (PI-adjusted) parameters predict mechanical complications after deformity surgery better than absolute targets.

## 4. Alignment targets (SRS-Schwab)
- **PI-LL mismatch under about 10 degrees** (LL roughly equal to PI ± 10 degrees).
- **PT under about 20 degrees.**
- **SVA under about 5 cm** (under 4 cm in the SRS-Schwab modifier).
- **Age-adjusted targets** (Lafage): older patients tolerate (and need) more positive alignment; **over-correction in the elderly increases proximal junctional kyphosis (PJK)**.

| SRS-Schwab sagittal modifier | 0 | + | ++ |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PI-LL** | Under 10 degrees | 10-20 | Over 20 |
| **PT** | Under 20 degrees | 20-30 | Over 30 |
| **SVA** | Under 4 cm | 4-9.5 cm | Over 9.5 cm |

- Coronal curve types: **T** (thoracic only, lumbar under 30), **L** (TL/lumbar only), **D** (double), **N** (no major coronal curve).

## 5. Roussouly classification of normal sagittal shapes
| Type | Sacral slope | Lordosis | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Under 35 degrees** | Short, low lordosis; long thoracolumbar kyphosis | Disc degeneration at the TL junction, posterior element impingement at L5-S1 |
| 2 | **Under 35 degrees** | Flat, long hypolordosis ("flat back") | **Disc herniation, early disc degeneration** |
| **3** | **35-45 degrees** | **Balanced, harmonious** (commonest) | |
| 4 | **Over 45 degrees** | Long, high lordosis | Facet arthritis, **spondylolysis**, posterior element overload |
| 3 anteverted | | | Variant with low PI and anteverted pelvis |

## 6. Compensation and decompensation
- **Stages:** (1) **thoracic hypokyphosis**, (2) **hyperextension of mobile lumbar segments** (can cause retrolisthesis, facet overload), (3) **pelvic retroversion (PT rises)**: the most important compensatory mechanism, limited by **hip extension reserve** (hip flexion contractures limit compensation), (4) **knee flexion** and ankle dorsiflexion (energy-expensive, "crouched" posture). When exhausted: **SVA becomes positive**, forward stoop, fatigue, inability to stand upright.
- **Flatback syndrome:** loss of lumbar lordosis after **distraction instrumentation (Harrington rods)** into the lumbar spine, after fusions in kyphosis, or degenerative; forward-leaning posture, knee flexion, back pain.
- **Hip-spine syndrome:** coexisting hip and spine pathology; **spinopelvic mobility affects THA**: a **stiff spine (fused or degenerative) with little pelvic tilt change between standing and sitting** raises the risk of **THA dislocation and impingement** (adjust cup anteversion/inclination; consider dual-mobility). **Sitting: pelvis normally tilts posteriorly (retroverts) about 20 degrees, increasing functional cup anteversion.** "Stuck sitting/stuck standing" pelvises.
- **Proximal junctional kyphosis (PJK):** **proximal junctional angle over 10 degrees and at least 10 degrees greater than pre-operatively** (Glattes). Risk factors: older age, osteoporosis, **large corrections**, over-correction relative to age-adjusted targets, fusion to the sacrum, **UIV at the thoracolumbar junction**, posterior ligament disruption, high BMI. Proximal junctional failure (fracture, instability, neurological deficit) needs revision. Prevention: teriparatide, tethers, transitional rods, cement augmentation at UIV, soft landing.

## 7. Corrective osteotomies
| Osteotomy | Schwab grade | Correction | Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Smith-Petersen / Ponte (posterior column)** | 1-2 | **About 10 degrees per level** (about 1 degree per mm of resection) | **Mobile anterior column (open disc)**; opening wedge anteriorly |
| **Pedicle subtraction osteotomy (PSO)** | 3 | **About 30-35 degrees** at one level | Fixed (fused) anterior column; three-column **closing wedge** through the vertebra (usually **L3**, below the conus) |
| Extended PSO / bone-disc-bone | 4 | About 35-45 degrees | Includes the disc |
| **Vertebral column resection (VCR)** | 5-6 | **Over 40 degrees**, multiplanar | Rigid, severe, angular deformity (congenital kyphoscoliosis, post-TB) ; **highest neurological risk** |

- **Ankylosing spondylitis chin-on-chest deformity:** lumbar PSO (L3) for global kyphosis; **cervicothoracic extension osteotomy (C7-T1)** for cervical kyphosis (C7 has a larger canal and the vertebral artery enters at C6); correct to restore horizontal gaze (**CBVA about 0-10 degrees**).

## 8. Clinical relevance summary
- **Degenerative spondylolisthesis/stenosis surgery:** restore segmental lordosis (especially L4-S1) during fusion; **interbody devices (ALIF/LLIF) give more lordosis than TLIF/PLIF**.
- **Fusing in kyphosis** leads to **adjacent segment disease** and flatback.
- **Lumbar fusion and THA:** fused lumbar spine increases THA dislocation risk; consider dual-mobility cups.
- **Children's isthmic spondylolisthesis:** high PI and high slip angle predict progression; reduction of high-grade slips (restores alignment but **L5 nerve root palsy** risk).

> Exam pearl: **PI = PT + SS. PI is fixed (morphological); PT and SS are positional. High PI = more lordosis needed and associated with isthmic spondylolisthesis.**

> Exam pearl: **Targets: PI-LL under 10 degrees, PT under 20, SVA under 5 cm (TPA under 20). Pelvic retroversion (high PT) is the key compensation; knee flexion is the last.** **Sagittal imbalance correlates best with disability.**

> Exam pearl: **Ponte/SPO about 10 degrees per level (needs a mobile disc), PSO about 30-35 degrees at one level (usually L3), VCR over 40 degrees (highest neuro risk).** **Stiff spine + THA = higher dislocation risk.**
